Plotting how well a model classifies ties

Source: R/plot_tests.R
plot.infernetConfusion.Rd

This plotting method is for the result of infernet::diagnose_confusion(), which compares the ties that a model of a binary outcome predicts with the ties that were observed. The S3 class is "infernetConfusion".

  • The ROC curve gives the true positive rate against the false positive rate at every threshold. The diagonal is a model that guesses, and the area under the curve (AUC) is in the title.

  • The confusion matrix gives the mean count of each cell over the draws of the predicted probabilities, with its 95% interval.

  • The metrics give the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1 on one scale from 0 to 1.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'infernetConfusion'
plot(x, panel = c("all", "roc", "confusion", "metrics"), ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class "infernetConfusion". For example, infernet::diagnose_confusion().

panel

By default "all", which shows the three panels together. "roc", "confusion", or "metrics" shows one panel.

...

Further arguments to be passed on to plot.

Value

A ggplot2 object, or a patchwork of three of them.

Examples

# Needs 'infernet' (https://github.com/stocnet/infernet)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  fit <- infernet::estimate_mrqap(. ~ ego(Age) + alter(Age),
                                  manynet::ison_adolescents |>
                                    manynet::mutate_nodes(Age = 12:19),
                                  times = 20, control = list(seed = 1))
  plot(infernet::diagnose_confusion(fit, times = 100))
} # }
